verdict.reasoning: Patient: "it's just aching all over, but, definitely the last six weeks... feeling really tired, run down."
Patient: "it probably coincided with some time around then. End of January, start of Feb." and "probably a couple of weeks after I got back." – referring to return from US holiday.
Patient: "yeah, sort of aching shoulders, back, the hips, knees" and to swelling: Doctor: "Any swelling that you've noticed?" Patient: "No".
Patient: "I don't have any rashes now, but there was... back of my calf" and "probably, uh, around the end of February, the middle to end of Feb... it faded over a couple of weeks."
Regarding the time of the rash: Doctor: "Did you have any fevers at that time?" Patient: "possibly a little bit feverish" and also mentions "it turns out it was a bit of a sore throat I had."
Doctor: "Any change in your weight at all?" Patient: "I'm probably less hungry, but no, no weight change" and confirms smaller portions.
Doctor asks about "persistent cold symptoms or earaches, sore throat, chest cough, shortness of breath, phlegm" and Patient replies "Uh, no."
At review of current symptoms patient denies sore throat when asked along with other ENT/respiratory symptoms: "Uh, no." Past sore throat tied to rash is described as prior, not current.
Doctor: "Any difficulty swallowing or acid in your throat, or abdominal pain?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Any change in your bowel habit, diarrhoea, vomiting or blood in the stool?" Patient: "Uh, no." (Covers absence of vomiting, diarrhea, overt blood.)
Doctor: "Any difficulty passing urine or blood in the urine?" Patient: "No, that's all fine."
Doctor: "any headaches, blurred vision, tingling, numbness?" Patient: "Um, no." (no focal neuro or visual symptoms).
After initially denying specific neuro symptoms, patient clarifies: "But it's the sort of headache maybe in just generally feeling a bit crappy." indicating mild nonspecific headaches.
Work: Patient: "I've been going to work. I don't know how effective it's been." Energy/exercise: "definitely sort of tired" and "I'm not exercising as I would normally."
Doctor asks about mental health/stress; Patient: "Pretty good at the moment, actually" and "I've... yeah, in a pretty good place."
Patient: "Asthma and hay fever if they can help."
Patient: "I've got one of those, um, preventative, I think" and later: "I have it. I've been using the everyday for the morning and night." (referring to preventer inhaler).
Patient: "I take, um, one of the antihistamines... I get that from, just from the pharmacy." – consistent with OTC antihistamines.
Work: Patient: "I work for a health technology company actually." Activity: "I do quite a lot of walking, and we did, um, quite a lot while we were out in the, on holiday as well."
Regarding US trip: Patient: "I was in shorts and, and boots" while walking.
Living situation: Patient: "just my wife." Alcohol: Doctor: "Drink any alcohol?" Patient: "Sorry, occasionally, that was."

Symptoms: "aching all over... last six weeks... feeling really tired" and timing post-travel: symptoms started "probably a couple of weeks after I got back" from US trip, consistent with fatigue and diffuse aches post-travel.

Rash: on calf in "middle to end of Feb"; exposure: "I do quite a lot of walking... on holiday as well" and "I was in shorts and, and boots"; bite: "I don't recall any bugs, I don't remember seeing anything bitten."
Doctor: "a bacterial infection... called lyme disease... we would do a test for" and "we would also check... which can cause reduced energy, tiredness and aching" with blood tests.

Doctor: "get some blood tests, checking all the normal things, like liver, kidneys, blood count, etc. But also... one which you can get which can produce a rash like that" (Lyme disease test). This implies FBC, U&E, LFTs, and Lyme serology.
No mention in the transcript of an additional 'fatigue screen' or protocol-based extra tests beyond the general labs and Lyme serology.
Doctor: "if [Lyme test] comes back positive, then there are specific antibiotics that we would give you to treat it."
Doctor: "if you book that through the support line" referring to arranging the blood tests.
Doctor: "when you've had the test arrange a follow up about a week after, after you've had the test done." This is a week after the test, not a week after results.
Opening: "it's Doctor Smith from Babylon" and nature of dialogue indicate teleconsult; no vitals or physical exam findings are documented.
Patient: "I don't have any rashes now, but there was... in fact I've got a photo, um, on my phone" and shows photo of rash on back of calf that "faded over a couple of weeks."
